BiblicalUsage: zâg means the skin of a grape. In Numbers 6:4 we read, "All the days of his separation shall he eat nothing that is made of the vine tree, from the kernels even to the husk."
TheologicalSignificance: zag is the skin of a grape, and I hold that even a word used only a few times carries weight where God placed it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
